Board redesign — three directions

Same data, three layouts. The board today renders members as rows × status as columns, which leaves most lanes empty and lets the Done column grow without bound or counts. Each direction below tackles that differently. Realistic data; live theme tokens.

Direction A

Refined swimlanes

Keeps the familiar member×status matrix but fixes the gaps: per-column counts, a search + status filter bar, a per-member progress bar, richer cards (kind chip, retry/review badges, status accent stripe), and a collapsible Done column so history stops dominating.

Direction B

Classic Kanban

Drops swimlanes for four status columns with prominent counts. The member moves onto the card as an assignee chip — better when most work is unassigned (it flows as one stream instead of empty rows). Failed cards get a red tint so they read at a glance; Done dims and collapses.

Direction C

Activity table

For scale (200 tasks): a dense, sortable, filterable list instead of a spatial board. Every row shows status, assignee, kind, last-update and duration in aligned columns you can sort by any field. Best for "what's happening right now and let me drill in," at the cost of the at-a-glance spatial grouping.
